biology.groups-describe.0001.all: saprotrophic nutrition: secrete extracellular digestive enzymes onto food; digest it outside the body; absorb soluble products (through hyphae)

biology.groups-describe-multi.0005.b: single cell; cell wall (not cellulose); cell membrane; cytoplasm; no nucleus, circular chromosome of DNA; plasmids; some have flagellum / slime capsule

biology.groups-explain.0004.all: viruses have no cell wall (protein coat instead); viruses are not living cells / reproduce inside host cells so antibiotics have nothing to target

biology.groups-explain-multi.0007.b: body made of mycelium of hyphae; cell walls of chitin; feeds by saprotrophic nutrition / extracellular digestion; contains many nuclei; stores glycogen

biology.groups-mcq-rev.0003.all: Multicellular, have no cell walls and often store carbohydrate as glycogen

biology.groups-recall.0005.all: protein coat; genetic material (DNA or RNA)

biology.heart-data-graph.0002.a: as running speed increases heart rate increases; roughly linear/proportional with data quote
biology.heart-data-graph.0002.b: muscles respire faster; need more oxygen and glucose delivered; more CO2 removed; heart pumps faster

biology.heart-data-pct.0002.b: more respiration in muscles; more O2/glucose needed; more CO2 removed; faster blood flow

biology.heart-data-plot.0003.a: axes with labels/units, sensible scale, points plotted correctly, line
biology.heart-data-plot.0003.b: as cholesterol increases risk increases; increase gets steeper (non-linear)

biology.heart-data-read.0001.c: more respiration in muscles; more oxygen/glucose needed; more CO2 removed

biology.heart-describe.0001.all: vena cava -> right atrium -> (tricuspid valve) right ventricle -> pulmonary artery -> lungs -> pulmonary vein -> left atrium -> (bicuspid) left ventricle -> aorta

biology.heart-describe-multi.0005.b: blood passes through heart twice per circuit; pulmonary circuit to lungs and back; systemic circuit to body and back; keeps high pressure

biology.heart-explain.0007.all: oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix; less oxygen delivered to tissues/cells; less aerobic respiration so less energy released

biology.heart-explain-multi.0001.a: high saturated fat/cholesterol diet; smoking; lack of exercise; high blood pressure; stress; genetics; obesity
biology.heart-explain-multi.0001.b: thick muscular wall to withstand high pressure; elastic tissue stretches and recoils to maintain pressure; narrow lumen maintains pressure

biology.heart-ext.0002.all: raises blood cholesterol; fatty deposits/plaque build up in coronary artery walls; lumen narrows; blood flow reduced / clot forms; less O2 and glucose to heart muscle; heart muscle cannot respire, dies -> heart attack
